human.controls: Arrows move. SPACE shoots or acts (games with a ShootAvatar or FlakAvatar).

reference.name: py-vgdl, Colas lineage, as ported to gymnasium by Tomov (language_and_experience @ dbp); infer-vgdl vendors the same engine plus GravityAvatar, DestroyAllBreakwalls and BothPlayersOnExit for picoparkish and tutorial
reference.block_size_note: play_human.py and src/utils.py run at block_size=50; 1 is the planning-only fast mode in which every fractional-speed sprite is frozen. The vgdl-metagen gate ran at 1. fmri-gym's vgdl backend wraps this same fork, so the DBP study's VGDL games are this corpus.
reference.parity: full state every step: time, score, ended, won, and every live sprite's (type, x, y, resources); same seed and action sequence; tests/gate_oracle.mjs vs tests/oracle.py
not_matched: pixels (py-vgdl draws sprites at block_size with pygame; PlayTrain draws 8px cells scaled into a 64x64 frame)
reward: PlayTrain reward is the score delta per step; infer-vgdl's gym wrapper is not the reference here

multi-key actions: the vgdl6 space holds one key per action, so py-vgdl's largest-combination tie-break (SPACE beats arrows when both are held) is never exercised; default8's LEFT_D/RIGHT_D would be, and are reproduced
the host reset consumes one NOOP frame before the first agent action (PlayTrain draws and steps in the same frame)
